## Citation

Kathe, S.D., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., Jaruga, P., Newton, M.R., Burrows, C.J., Bandaru, V., Dizdaroglu, M., Bond, J.P., & Wallace, S.S. (2009). Plant and Fungal Fpg Homologs are Formamidopyrimidine DNA Glycosylases but not 8-Oxoguanine DNA Glycosylases. *DNA Repair*, 8(5), 643-653.

## Abstract

The formamidopyrimidine DNA glycosylase (Fpg) family removes oxidized purines from damaged DNA. This study characterizes plant and fungal Fpg homologs to determine substrate specificity and functional conservation across eukaryotic organisms.

## Key Findings

- Plant and fungal Fpg homologs efficiently remove formamidopyrimidines (FaPy lesions)
- These enzymes show reduced activity toward 8-oxoguanine, unlike bacterial Fpg
- Substrate preference differences reflect evolutionary adaptation to cellular environments
- Results clarify the functional evolution of BER enzymes across domains of life

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed bioinformatics analysis and evolutionary comparisons of Fpg protein sequences.
